title: Increasing Decreasing String
summary: Given a string s, reorder it by first removing and appending the smallest character greater than the last appended character, then removing and appending the largest character smaller than the last appended character, until all characters are removed.
statement: Given a string s, reorder it by first removing and appending the smallest character greater than the last appended character, then removing and appending the largest character smaller than the last appended character, until all characters are removed. Repeat this process ensuring to choose any occurrence of the smallest or largest character if it appears more than once.
constraints: Each ascending and descending pass uses at most one copy of each remaining character.
hints: Character counts avoid repeatedly sorting every occurrence.
On an ascending pass visit keys smallest to largest and consume one available copy; then visit largest to smallest.
Repeat the two passes until output length equals input length.
Each pass follows the required next-greater or next-smaller choice exactly.
editorial: Each pass follows the required next-greater or next-smaller choice exactly.

tests.explanation: Alternating distinct-character passes produce abccba twice.
The ascending pass consumes a,r,t, so the result is art.
